note: The test club's statuses and comments for the reseeded season (D313), by competition key (lib/testClub.ts seasonPlan). A status is the card's own player's, at most 140 characters; a comment is anybody's on a card in that competition, at most 280. Innuendo is fine (Ross, 24 Nov 2026); no slurs, nothing explicit. Results are never asserted — the cards are made on the day, so a line talks about the round, not the board.

statuses.paddy: Kept the hands quiet through impact all day. Lag is everything, people. LAG.
statuses.jed: Medal play is the purest form of the game. The Greeks would have approved. Of my front nine, at least.
statuses.gob: Course was rigged. Holes visibly smaller than regulation. I've measured mine.
statuses.elaine: Birdies. Plural. Somebody get me a drink and a man who can count.
statuses.pierce: Disappointed in the greenkeeping. Wrote a strongly worded letter. To myself. On club stationery I paid for.

comments.text: Nobody asked about your lag, Paddy.
Gob, your takeaway is so far inside you're practically hugging yourself. Feet together, half swings, two hundred balls. You're welcome.
He did measure it. Please don't ask him how.
The Greeks also didn't take a mulligan on the 4th, sir. I was standing right there.
Such a lovely round, Mr President! Do you always play with the same security detail? Just curious how many of them there are. For the fourball.
Ladies' tees moved forward again, I see. Easy to make birdies when you start halfway to the green.
Tom, her tees are forty yards shorter and her handicap is ten shots lower than yours. Run the numbers. Actually don't, it'll only upset you.
A letter to yourself is still the most anyone has ever read of your work, Pierce.
Not bad, Sloan. Not bad at all for a girl.
Pierce, check the board before you type. Then don't.
He's not angry at the course. He's angry he brought an audience.

statuses.tom: In my day you couldn't get a buggy round here. You walked, you suffered, you liked it. Today I suffered.
statuses.pierce: Two-man field. One gentleman, one Tom. You do the maths.

comments.text: Tom, that number would get a quiz show cancelled. Maybe the buggy wasn't the problem.
Pierce, a field of two isn't a field. It's a date.
Fun fact: Old Tom Morris won the Open four times. Different Tom. Clearly.
Congratulations on beating a man who designed half the bunkers here and still can't get out of them.

statuses.michael: Played in front of my brother's ego all day. It played better than I did.
statuses.gob: Illusionist's tip: if the ball isn't in the hole, it was never really there. Fourteen lost balls. Fourteen illusions.
statuses.paddy: Swing felt long and loose. Too loose. Back to the range.
statuses.pierce: Hot day for Pierce Hawthorne. Some of these young men could learn a thing or two from my tempo.

comments.text: Rough day, Michael? Maybe stick to running the family business into the ground.
Gob, two of those fourteen balls were mine. You borrowed my balls on the 3rd. I'd like them back.
Paddy, Hogan said the secret is in the dirt. You appear to have found all of it.
Jed, your grip is so strong the club is filing a complaint. Turn the left hand back two knuckles, and stop talking at the top of the backswing.
Pierce scored well. Statistically, even a stopped clock makes the odd birdie.
Lovely to see the ladies giving it a go on a Saturday. In my day Saturday was for golf.
It was golf, Tom. In your day the shafts were wooden and so was the sense of humour. Bring at least one of them up to date.
Best tempo in the club, Pierce. Shame about the man.

statuses.jed: President's Prize. A President, prized. Four on the last. Some would call it destiny.
statuses.cj: Spent four hours watching my boss find balls that were demonstrably lost. Ask me about the 18th. Actually, don't.
statuses.don: Played well. Drank well. Didn't have to go home until six.
statuses.gob: Trick shot off the 7th tee. Ball's still in the air. Waiting on it.
statuses.tom: Grand old competition, ruined by people photographing their sandwiches at the turn.
statuses.pierce: Somebody dented my Bentley. If it was a golf ball, I want it found. Unlike Jed's.

comments.text: Sir, the ball went into the gorse on 18. I watched it go in. The gorse watched it go in. A four on that hole isn't destiny, it's a cover-up.
Rule 18.2: a ball is lost after three minutes of searching. I searched for two minutes and fifty-eight seconds. History will vindicate me.
What a finish, Jed! Who carries your bag on the 18th — always the same agent, or does the rota change at night? I'd love to thank them personally.
Played with you, Jed. Your drive on 18 went left of left. Your four went left of the rules.
The second ball always plays better. Ask anyone who's been married.
For the record, the ball came down. In the car park. On Pierce's Bentley.
A lady secretary playing in the President's Prize. In my day they wouldn't let one past the door, never mind the 1st tee.
Tom, I've briefed the world's press with a root canal. Your opinion is a light breeze.

statuses.elaine: Ladies' day. No men, no mansplaining, no Pierce. Best four hours of my month.
statuses.sloan: Long game up on the month. Yes, I keep a spreadsheet. Yes, it has tabs.
statuses.elizabeth: Lovely morning with the girls. So much to talk about!
statuses.cj: Played like I brief the press on the budget. Lots of words, very little in the hole.

comments.text: Elizabeth, you asked me nine questions about the West Wing floor plan between the 3rd and the 7th. Is everything alright at home?
Only making conversation, CJ! Which door does the President usually use at 7am? For my diary.
Ladies' day midweek. Sensible. Keeps the course clear for those of us who actually pay for it.
Tom, the women pay the same subscription and replace more divots. I have receipts and a pivot table.
Elaine, if you ever need a man to show you a proper short game, my door is always open.
Pierce, your door's always open because nobody has ever walked through it.
Lovely pace on the putts, Sloan. Now — that left wrist at the top. We need to talk.

statuses.tom: Captain's Prize, and the old boy shows them how it's done. Hickory spirit, steel shafts.
statuses.jed: The Captain's Prize is named for the captain, who is not me — a constitutional anomaly I will be addressing.
statuses.gob: Captain asked me not to do the dove thing on the 1st tee again. Did the dove thing on the 2nd.
statuses.paddy: Bad day. Posted my swing video in the group chat for analysis. Nobody replied.

comments.text: Decent card, Tom. My model says the last time you put one like that together, Truman was in office.
Sir, you have no jurisdiction over the club constitution. You have a 3 handicap that's out on parole.
The dove is fine, everyone. The captain is not. Sorry, captain.
Paddy, I'd analyse your swing, but you'd only take it as an insult. Like I do.
Watched the video, Paddy. Your hips fire before your shoulders. Also you filmed it vertically, which is a war crime.
Michael, a word to the wise: you'll never get anywhere in this club by being reasonable.
Thanks, Pierce. Noted, and ignored.
Don, you strike me as a man who keeps secrets. Do you happen to know anyone in government?

statuses.elaine: Played with Jed and CJ. Jed explained the Rules of Golf to me eleven times. He's still explaining. I've gone home.
statuses.don: Went round in the time it takes some men to find their ball. Then had a Scotch.
statuses.pierce: Medal play is a test of character. I passed. The scorecard didn't.
statuses.michael: Kept it in play. Kept the family out of it. A good day.

comments.text: Elaine, in 1744 the Gentlemen Golfers of Leith wrote thirteen rules. Thirteen! I have memorised all of them, and invented four more.
And all four of yours are about you being given a gimme.
Tough round today, CJ! Are you sleeping? Late nights in the Situation Room? How late, roughly? Which nights?
Elizabeth, that's the fourth week running you've asked. I've started a file. On you.
Pierce, you have the character of a man with a chequebook. Medal play wants a man with a putter.
The scorecard has a character too, Pierce. It's a crime scene.
Gob, you're swaying off the ball like a man in a tight corridor. Stay centred. Turn, don't slide.
I sway because the crowd moves me, Paddy. Something you wouldn't know.
Don, how are you always so calm out there?
Because I'm not out there, Michael.

statuses.cj: Points. Lots of them. If the President wishes to discuss it, he can make an appointment.
statuses.gob: Retiring from golf. Back next Saturday.
statuses.tom: Old Tom still has it. Where 'it' is the only working knee left in this group.
statuses.paddy: Lost my swing. If found, please return. Answers to 'one plane'.

comments.text: CJ, an outstanding round. No President has ever been prouder of his staff.
Sir, please be proud quietly. There's a pool reporter in the bar.
He retires every week. Next Saturday he'll come back billed as 'the comeback'.
Retiring is the first thing he's done all day with any conviction.
Paddy lost his swing. I've been asked to find it. And — ta-da — it's in the bin.
Good round, Tom. Funny how well it goes the week you don't complain about the ladies' tees.
I complained, Sloan. I simply complained quietly. Like a gentleman.
Quietly, Tom. On a public feed. With your name on it.
Pierce, you shot a number. That's all I can say without a lawyer present.
Congratulations CJ! Shall we celebrate? Your place? Bring your work laptop, I'd love to see what you're working on!
